which only uses 50 parallel preconditioned Jacobi iterations

issues.failure_explanation: All theorems treat $y^n$ as the exact solution of the proximal subproblem with a fixed positive semidefinite $M$. By Proposition 1 this corresponds to exactly one preconditioned step. Nothing is proved for several inner iterations, which correspond to a different effective preconditioner $\mathbb M_k$. The paper does not show that the associated $M_k=\mathbb M_k-T$ is positive semidefinite, nor that it is a symmetric proximal weight at all. Yet the abstract, the introduction and the experiments (50 Jacobi sweeps) rely on this claim. The word 'feasible' is also undefined.

failure_location.quote: It is important to note that we will prove that any finite and feasible preconditioned iterations can ensure the global convergence of the whole nonlinear second-order convex splitting method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short lemma showing that $k$ steps of a stationary iteration with $\mathbb M\succeq T$ (SGS, Jacobi, Richardson) equal one step with an effective symmetric $M_k\succeq 0$. Restrict the claim to these preconditioners, or restate it as a single-step result.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of global convergence 'without error control' after finitely many inner iterations is not established. The experiments that use 50 Jacobi sweeps are not covered by the theory.
issues.title: Unproved claim that any finite number of preconditioned iterations preserves global convergence
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma and a narrower statement suffice, with no new global architecture. It is more than a wording fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs $\|\nabla E^n(z)-\nabla E^n(y^n)\|\le(\beta-\alpha)\|d^n\|$ with $\beta=\frac{2}{3\delta t}-L$. This requires the unstated hypothesis $\alpha<\frac{2}{3\delta t}-L$ (more generally $\alpha<\frac{2}{3\delta t}-L+\lambda_{\min}(M)$). The symbol $\beta$ is also reused for the backtracking factor. The algorithm lets $\alpha>0$ be arbitrary, so the WHILE loop in Step 6 is not guaranteed to terminate. In the experiments $\delta t=6-10^{-15}$ and $L=1/9$ give $\frac{2}{3\delta t}-L\approx 0$, while $\alpha=0.2$.

failure_location.quote: there is some small $\delta > 0$ and $\beta = \frac{2}{3\delta t} - L$, such that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis $\alpha<\frac{2}{3\delta t}-L+\lambda_{\min}(M)$ in the lemma and the algorithm. Rename the clashing $\beta$. Choose experimental parameters accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Well-definedness of the line search, and the energy-decrease inequality used in all convergence results, is not guaranteed for the algorithm as stated. It also fails for the parameters used in the experiments.
issues.title: Line-search feasibility needs alpha below 2/(3 dt) - L (plus lambda_min(M)); the algorithm and experiments allow arbitrary alpha
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard parameter condition repairs the proof and keeps the method and conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition $(1+\lambda_{\max})^2=\frac{4}{3\delta tL}-\frac12$, so $c(\lambda_{\max},\delta t,L)=0$ exactly. The constant $\frac{\alpha\lambda_{\min}+c(\lambda_{\max},\delta t,L)}{(1+\lambda_{\max})^2}$ then equals $\frac{\alpha\lambda_{\min}}{(1+\lambda_{\max})^2}$. This is zero when $\lambda_{\min}=0$, which is allowed since $\lambda_n\ge0$ and backtracking can give arbitrarily small or zero steps. The hypothesis $\lambda_n<\lambda_{\max}$ is only pointwise, so $\sup_n\lambda_n$ may equal $\lambda_{\max}$. The displayed bound $\sum\|u^{n+1}-u^n\|^2\le\frac{(1+\lambda_{\max})^2}{\alpha\lambda_{\min}+c(\lambda_{\max},\delta t,L)}(\cdots)$ then has a zero denominator. The constant $\tilde C$ in Theorem 1 and the appendix inherits this.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $\lambda_n\le\bar\lambda<\lambda_{\max}$ uniformly and use $c(\bar\lambda,\delta t,L)>0$ in the constant. The $\alpha\lambda_{\min}$ term can be dropped.
issues.overall_effect: Square-summability, the finite-length argument and the rates are not proved in the stated regime. The threshold $\lambda_{\max}$ is attained or exceeded in the limit.
issues.title: Summability constant vanishes at lambda_max, and lambda_min may be 0
issues.why_classification: A uniform strict bound on the step sizes, enforced through the algorithm parameter, fixes the constant with a local change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: rather than a maximum searching step ($\lambda_n:= \bar \lambda_{\max}$)

issues.failure_explanation: The quadratic $a\lambda^2+b\lambda+c$ has its minimiser at $-b/(2a)$, so the formula for $\lambda_n^*$ is missing a minus sign. With $e_n'(0)<0$ and positive curvature as written it is negative. Moreover, $\max\{\bar\lambda_{\max},\lambda_n^*\}\ge\bar\lambda_{\max}$, so the initial step is never reduced. This contradicts the stated aim of starting from a more precise point instead of the maximal step. It can also push $\lambda_n$ beyond the thresholds required by the convergence theorems.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $\lambda_n^*=-e_n'(0)\bar\lambda^2/(2(e_n(\bar\lambda)-e_n(0)-\bar\lambda e_n'(0)))$ and start backtracking from $\min\{\bar\lambda_{\max},\lambda_n^*\}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed accelerated initial step is not a valid, well-defined safeguard and can violate the step-size bounds on which the convergence theory relies.
issues.title: Quadratic-interpolation initial step: wrong sign of minimiser and max used instead of min
issues.why_classification: A local two-symbol correction restores the intended procedure and keeps the guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Additionally, we make the assumption that the energy $E(x)$ is level-bounded

issues.failure_explanation: The remark only verifies the KL property. The theorems also need level-boundedness of $E$ and a globally Lipschitz $\nabla F$. For the SCAD model $m<k$, so $\ker A\neq\{0\}$. Along $u=tv$ with $v\in\ker A$, the penalty $P_M$ is constant for large $t$, so $E$ stays bounded and some sublevel sets are unbounded. Level-boundedness therefore fails and boundedness of the iterates is not available. For the Ginzburg-Landau model $F=\frac1\epsilon\mathbb W$ has gradient $\frac1\epsilon(u^3-u)$, which is not globally Lipschitz. The step-size condition $\delta t<\frac{2}{3L}$ and the estimates in all proofs therefore have no valid constant $L$.

failure_location.quote: the global convergence of these two models thus follows

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For SCAD, add a coercive term or assume bounded iterates, or restrict to $\ker A=\{0\}$. For Ginzburg-Landau, prove an a priori bound and use a Lipschitz constant on the resulting bounded set, or modify the double-well function. Then restate the claim accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted convergence guarantees for the two experimental models are unsupported. The theory does not cover the SCAD experiment as posed, and covers the Ginzburg-Landau experiment only after an additional a priori bound.
issues.title: Global convergence claimed for SCAD and Ginzburg-Landau models without verifying level-boundedness and Lipschitz hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The general theorems survive, but each model needs a separate contained argument or a modified model. For SCAD, boundedness of the iterates is lost without a change to the model.

issues.failure_explanation: With $L=1/9$ and $\delta t\approx 6$, the thresholds are $\lambda_{\max}=\sqrt{3/2}-1\approx0.22$ for $\hat u^n=u^n$. For $\hat u^n=\tilde u^n$ the bound is $\min\{\sqrt{3/2}-1,\sqrt5-1\}\approx0.22$. The experiments start the line search at $\bar\lambda_{\max}=5$, with $\alpha=0.2$ as well. Nothing in the algorithm forces $\lambda_n$ below the thresholds. The theorems' hypotheses are therefore violated by the tested configurations, yet the paper presents these runs as covered by the global convergence results.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either run with $\bar\lambda_{\max}$, $\delta t$ and $\alpha$ satisfying the theorems' conditions, or state explicitly that the large-step experiments are heuristic and not covered by the proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The reported BapDCA$_{\text{ls}}$ results come from parameter choices outside the proven regime, so the guarantee of global convergence does not apply to them.
issues.title: Experimental parameters violate the step-size thresholds required by the convergence theorems
issues.why_classification: Qualifying the claim or re-choosing parameters repairs the mismatch without changing any theorem or method.
